note: The id/placeholder audit (`script/m14/tmp/elixir-id-integrity.ts`) re-measured EX-D9's claim — 'a visible `Unknown` placeholder is never a missed STATIC NAME' — over 559 files / 10,745 symbols of the elixir repo, four corpora after the claim was made. Result: 20 `Unknown` symbols, 19 of them genuinely dynamic (`def unquote(name)(…)`, `def unquote(:"weirdly named/fun-")`, ExUnit's `unquote(:"property is true")`), and **exactly ONE a missed static name**: `defmacro (..)`, Kernel's own zero-arity range operator (elixir/lib/elixir/lib/kernel.ex:4347). The grammar shapes that name as `arguments > block > operator_identifier`, which no signature branch recognised, so the definition fell through to the EX-D9 placeholder — and a second parenthesized operator in the same module MERGED into the same placeholder row (both arity 0), so one real definition was invisible and one row stood for two. Fix: the operator token is statically nameable, so it is named, with the parameter list read from the sibling `arguments` node when the form carries one (`def (op)(a, b)` is an ERROR node in this grammar but its argument list is readable) and a single `operand` when it does not. A genuinely dynamic name stays `Unknown` — pinned in the FORBID half below, because a placeholder is a claim and the fixture must say where it is still allowed. The placeholder is pinned POSITIVELY here (exactly one, a function, owned by the module): the pre-fix state published `defmacro (..)` as a placeholder MACRO and let a second parenthesized operator merge into the same row, so the count and the kind are the pins, not the name's absence.
